title: This Philosophy has the Power to DESTROY the World (Morality)
summary: Educated Barbarian episode on Nietzsche's view of morality (Beyond Good and Evil): morality is man-made, plural, rooted in will to power and the natural need for long obedience, and most people live in Kant's 'state of minority' without questioning it. He argues humans are born without a moral code, that freedom is self-imposed restriction, and that seeing morality from outside could dissolve social bonds, hence the title.
claims: Everyone follows some morality and it shapes how they live; if it is toxic, the only fix is to fix your morality
Following Nietzsche, morality is man-made and lives only through its human hosts, like a parasite or symbiont, so studying a group's morality reveals its character
Morality predates religion; religion crystallized existing tenets such as not killing into strict, widespread rules and laws
Atheists raised in Christian countries argue from Christian morality without realizing it
Systems of morality arise whenever humans form societies; in Europe morality mainly pacified violence so stable governments and families could exist
Kant's state of minority is the inability to think for oneself; most people stay there because it is comfortable, and anyone could leave it but most lack the courage
Society needs most people in a state of minority to function, but as an individual you are better off transcending it
Morality evolves over time and should be studied as a historical echo of the people who made it
There is no universal basis of morality, only moralities in the plural; philosophers who tried produced Eurocentric ethics
At the heart of every morality is will to power
Morality makes you forget it is external, so you treat it as part of you and offload responsibility onto it
Humans are born without a code of conduct, which statistically leads to bad acts; the very existence of morality proves we need correcting
Original sin is an allegory for the evil inside humans; evolution through war shows violence is in our blood
Every morality is a sign language of the emotions, not facts; the French Revolution read morally hides that the bourgeoisie manipulated commoners to replace the nobility
All morality is a tyranny against nature and reason, but that is no objection as long as you know why you submit to it
Stoicism is a self-imposed tyranny that benefits you only if you understand why you do it; YouTube stoics mostly don't
Freedom is unnatural: it is the limits you impose on yourself, while living by instinct with no limits is the life of an animal
The Ubermensch does not reject morality; he understands where his rules come from so he can use them
Following Nietzsche, long obedience in the same direction is the natural moral imperative; the question is whom you obey
Like wolves made into dogs, Christian morality domesticated vigorous European men until they lost their vigor; but going back to the beast is not the answer
The Industrial Revolution exploited the instinct to obey to make people into workers; today's anti-work sentiment is the backlash
Someone born evil who does good deserves more respect than someone who is good by nature
Emotion is the language of the state of minority, logic the language of majority
Charity and parenting are often expressions of will to power: the giver feels powerful and gets angry when help is refused
Using morality for your own benefit and favoring your interests is not bad unless you follow a morality that declares will to power bad
